# Esther Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 458v–459r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_009_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** Now in the twelfth month — the month of Adar — on the thirteenth day, when the king's command and edict were to be carried out, on the very day when the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, the reverse occurred: the Jews themselves overpowered those who hated them.

**2** The Jews assembled in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to strike against those who sought to harm them, and no one could withstand them, for the fear of them had fallen on all peoples. **3** All the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and the royal agents supported the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them. **4** For Mordecai was powerful in the king's court, and his fame spread throughout all the provinces, as the man Mordecai grew ever greater.

**5** The Jews struck down all their enemies with the sword, with slaughter and destruction, and did as they pleased to those who hated them.

**6** In the citadel of Susa the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men. **7** They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, **8** Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, **9** Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha — **10** the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

**11** That day the number of those killed in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king. **12** The king said to Queen Esther, "In the citadel of Susa the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman. What then have they done in the rest of the king's provinces! What is your petition? It shall be granted. What further is your request? It shall be done."

**13** Esther said, "If it please the king, let the Jews who are in Susa be permitted tomorrow also to act according to today's edict, and let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows." **14** The king commanded this to be done. A decree was issued in Susa, and the ten sons of Haman were hanged.

**15** The Jews in Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred men in Susa, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

**16** The rest of the Jews in the king's provinces assembled and defended their lives, and found relief from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder. **17** This was on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

**18** But the Jews in Susa assembled on both the thirteenth and the fourteenth days, and rested on the fifteenth day, making it a day of feasting and gladness.

**19** Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in unwalled towns, observe the fourteenth day of the month of Adar as a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday, and a day for sending gifts of food to one another.

**20** Mordecai recorded these events and sent letters to all the Jews throughout the provinces of King Ahasuerus, both near and far, **21** establishing for them that they should observe the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar, year after year, **22** as the days on which the Jews found rest from their enemies, and as the month that was turned for them from sorrow to gladness and from mourning to celebration — that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, of sending portions of food to one another and gifts to the poor.

**23** The Jews accepted what they had begun to do and what Mordecai had written to them. **24** For Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast Pur — that is, the lot — to crush and destroy them. **25** But when the matter came before the king, he gave orders in writing that the wicked plot Haman had devised against the Jews should come back on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

**26** Therefore they called these days Purim, after the word Pur. Because of all that was written in this letter, and what they had witnessed, and what had befallen them, **27** the Jews established and accepted for themselves, for their descendants, and for all who would join them, an obligation that should not be revoked: to observe these two days according to their written instructions and appointed time, every year, **28** so that these days should be remembered and observed in every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should never pass away from among the Jews, nor their memory perish from their descendants.

**29** Then Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter of Purim. **30** Letters were sent to all the Jews in the one hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, with words of peace and truth, **31** confirming these days of Purim at their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established for them, and as they had established for themselves and their descendants, with regard to the fasts and their lamentations. **32** The command of Esther confirmed these practices of Purim, and it was written in the book.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 9 is the longest in Esther and serves a dual function: it narrates the military resolution (vv. 1-19) and then transitions to the formal establishment of Purim as a perpetual festival (vv. 20-32). The council achieved broad agreement on most of this chapter. The key phrase *ve-nahafokh hu* ("the reverse occurred") was unanimously recognized as the thematic center of the entire book. All three translators preserved the threefold refrain about not touching the plunder, recognizing its theological weight. The listing of Haman's ten sons (vv. 7-9) follows the Masoretic tradition of writing these names in a distinctive columnar format in Torah scrolls — a visual emphasis the text format cannot fully reproduce. The transition from narrative to legislative language in verses 20-32 marks a shift in genre, and the council agreed to maintain the formal, decree-like tone of the Hebrew in the second half of the chapter.

---
## Disagreement Log

**v.1 — "the reverse occurred" vs. "the tables were completely turned"**
- **EMET:** "it was reversed" / **LOGOS:** "the reverse occurred" / **PNEUMA:** "the tables were completely turned"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the reverse occurred" — formal and precise. PNEUMA's idiomatic rendering is vivid but introduces a metaphor ("tables turned") absent from the Hebrew. EMET's version is grammatically awkward in English.

**v.13 — "let them hang" — public display of already-dead bodies**
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows" / **PNEUMA:** "let the bodies of Haman's ten sons be displayed on the gallows"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "let the ten sons of Haman be hanged on the gallows" — the Hebrew *yitlu* simply says "let them hang." PNEUMA's interpretive addition of "bodies" and "displayed" clarifies that they were already dead (v.10), but the consensus follows the Hebrew's own ambiguity.

**v.30 — "peace and truth" vs. "peace and faithfulness"**
- **EMET:** "peace and truth" (*shalom ve-emet*) / **LOGOS:** "peace and truth" / **PNEUMA:** "peace and faithfulness"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "peace and truth" — *emet* primarily means "truth/reliability/faithfulness." In this diplomatic context, "truth" better captures the formal register of official correspondence. "Faithfulness" leans toward covenantal theology not invoked here.

---

*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
